agent_evaluations.detailed_rationale: This evaluation FAILS radiology interpretation standards for multiple critical reasons: (1) No systematic interpretation approach demonstrated - content consists only of OSCE scenario metadata without actual imaging interpretation using ABCDE (CXR), 7-step (ECG), or ABC (CT) frameworks; (2) Clinical images are placeholder descriptions (e.g., 'Thyroid_Function_Tests for assessment') rather than actual interpretable radiological findings; (3) No image quality assessment performed (rotation, penetration, inspiration not evaluated); (4) Missing all core radiology content - no consolidation patterns, pneumothorax identification, ECG rhythm analysis, CT density assessment, or differential diagnoses provided; (5) No correlation between imaging findings and clinical presentation. While RAG citations meet minimum confidence thresholds and Australian terminology is used appropriately in scenario descriptions, the complete absence of actual radiological interpretation content makes this unsuitable for AMC Clinical Examination preparation. Manual review REQUIRED to determine if actual imaging content exists elsewhere or if this requires complete regeneration with systematic interpretation frameworks applied to each OSCE station.

violations.issue: For hyperkalemia OSCE (GAST-OSCE-0042), no emergency medication protocol provided
violations.suggested_fix: MUST include Australian-standard hyperkalemia treatment protocol: (1) Calcium gluconate 10% 10mL IV over 2-3 min (membrane stabilization), (2) Insulin-dextrose: 10 units Actrapid in 50mL 50% glucose IV (intracellular K+ shift), (3) Salbutamol 10-20mg nebulized (NOT albuterol - Australian name mandatory), (4) Sodium bicarbonate 50mmol IV if acidotic (pH <7.2), (5) Resonium 15g PO/PR (GI K+ binding), (6) Consider dialysis if K+ >7.0 or refractory

agent_evaluations.evaluation_notes: This document is an OSCE metadata structure containing 52 OSCE scenarios but lacks actual clinical content including medication management protocols. As medication-management-expert, I cannot evaluate medication appropriateness because no medications are prescribed or discussed in the content. The document requires substantial development before medication management evaluation is possible. Specific attention needed for: (1) Emergency medication protocols (hyperkalemia, DKA, hypoglycemia), (2) Chronic disease management medications (thyroid disorders, diabetes, AF anticoagulation), (3) Australian drug nomenclature enforcement (paracetamol NOT acetaminophen, adrenaline NOT epinephrine, salbutamol NOT albuterol), (4) PBS compliance for all prescribed medications, (5) Renal/hepatic dosing adjustments, (6) Drug interaction screening, (7) STOPP/START criteria for elderly patients. Recommend delegating to clinical-documentation-expert to create full OSCE scripts, then return to medication-management-expert for pharmacotherapy validation.
